criteria.statement: writeLocaleFileTree reports the paths it actually wrote, repo-root-relative with forward slashes, so the GitHub Action can stage that list verbatim instead of re-deriving it from the server's tree keys
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/pull.test.ts::writeLocaleFileTree > reports the paths it wrote, matching the tree keys for a plain JS project

criteria.statement: For a TypeScript project the reported path is locales/loader.ts — the file that exists — and never the locales/loader.js key the server sent. This is the loader bug: the Action staged the key, so every TypeScript customer committed an untyped loader.js while the loader.ts their app imports went unstaged
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/pull.test.ts::writeLocaleFileTree > reports loader.ts — not the loader.js key the server sent — for a TypeScript project

criteria.statement: A loader.js (and loader.d.ts) superseded by writing loader.ts is reported as removed, so the Action can stage the deletion and the obsolete file leaves the repository rather than staying committed forever
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/pull.test.ts::writeLocaleFileTree > reports a superseded loader.js as removed so the Action can stage the deletion

criteria.statement: Nothing is reported as removed when there was no stale loader to delete, so the Action is never asked to stage a deletion for a path that was already absent
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/pull.test.ts::writeLocaleFileTree > reports nothing removed when there was no stale loader to delete

criteria.statement: A tree key that would write outside the repository root is refused, and the whole tree is validated before anything is written so a bad key aborts rather than leaving a half-applied update behind. The tree is server-supplied and lands in a checkout where the Action holds contents: write, so a key of ../../.github/workflows/deploy.yml would otherwise be written and committed
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/pull.test.ts::writeLocaleFileTree > refuses a key that escapes the repository root, writing nothing

criteria.statement: Absolute keys are refused as well as relative escapes
A traversal segment in the middle of a key is caught, not only a leading one
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/pull.test.ts::writeLocaleFileTree > refuses a key that escapes via a traversal segment in the middle

criteria.statement: A traversal segment that resolves back inside the root is allowed, and the reported path is the resolved one — `git add app/../locales/en.json` would otherwise be asked to walk an app/ directory that need not exist
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/pull.test.ts::writeLocaleFileTree > allows a traversal segment that stays inside the root, and reports the resolved path

criteria.statement: The result file the Action reads carries writtenPaths and removedPaths per app, describing files on disk rather than the request that produced them
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/translate.test.ts::translate() result file for the GitHub Action > reports the paths written to disk, not the keys the server sent

criteria.statement: removedPaths is omitted entirely when nothing was deleted, so the Action can treat its presence as meaningful
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/translate.test.ts::translate() result file for the GitHub Action > omits removedPaths entirely when nothing was deleted

criteria.statement: In a monorepo each app's written paths are recorded against that app's own appDir, rather than collapsing to whichever app was processed first
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/translate.test.ts::translate() result file for the GitHub Action > records each monorepo app's own written paths against its own appDir

criteria.statement: The result file is written only after the locale files exist on disk. The previous order recorded the result first, which for this change would publish a path list before knowing whether those paths landed
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/translate.test.ts::translate() result file for the GitHub Action > writes the result only after the files exist on disk

criteria.statement: Orphaned locale files — present on disk but no longer a target — are reported as repo-root-relative paths alongside the existing warning, so the Action can repeat them as a CI annotation. They are reported and never deleted: the same test also matches a file a developer added by hand, and `vocoder clean` remains the deliberate local way to remove them

evidence.ref: warnOrphanedLocaleFiles in packages/cli/src/commands/translate.ts now returns the orphan list and writeTranslateResult serializes it as a top-level orphanedPaths key, omitted when empty. No deletion path was added to product code: in `git diff main...HEAD` the only rmSync lines under packages/cli/src/commands/ are context lines — the pre-existing loader.js and loader.d.ts cleanup in pull.ts, unchanged in behaviour. The two added rmSync calls are both in test teardown, removing the temporary RUNNER_TEMP directory. Consuming the annotation is the translate-action half of this ticket.

criteria.statement: Before this change the CLI/Action result contract had no test coverage at all, so the disagreement between the two halves could not have been caught by the suite

evidence.ref: Every pre-existing test in translate.test.ts runs under `delete process.env.GITHUB_ACTIONS` in its beforeEach (:412), and writeTranslateResult returns immediately when that variable is unset — so no test had ever caused the result file to be written, and `grep -n 'vocoder-result' src/__tests__/` returned nothing. The new describe block sets GITHUB_ACTIONS and points RUNNER_TEMP at a temporary directory, then reads the real file back. The ordering criterion AC12 was mutation-checked by hoisting writeTranslateResult above the write on the cached path: the suite reported `1 failed | 23 skipped`, failing exactly that criterion.
